security_audit.summary: The memory workflow itself is documentation-only and the apparent shell-execution findings in SKILL.md are Markdown false positives. However, the installation guide instructs users to disable TLS verification and execute base64-decoded remote content, which is a critical remote-code-execution risk. It also includes irreversible database deletion and an unscoped port-kill command.

remediation.issue: Installation downloads and executes unverified remote content with TLS verification disabled.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the curl-to-Node command. Distribute versioned, checksummed or signed artifacts through the documented repository install path, and keep TLS verification enabled.

remediation.issue: Reset instructions use recursive deletion of a persistent database directory.
remediation.suggestion: Require an instance-specific confirmation, show the resolved target, and offer a backup command before deletion.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting kills every process on port 3100.
remediation.suggestion: Identify the managed Paperclip process before stopping it, or direct users to pnpm dev:stop.

content.user_title: Organize Persistent Memory with PARA Files
content.value_statement: Agents can lose useful context between sessions and accumulate unstructured notes. This skill stores durable facts, daily events, and user preferences in a searchable PARA file system.
actual_capabilities: Organizes durable facts into Projects, Areas, Resources, and Archives folders.
Stores concise entity summaries and atomic YAML facts.
Records chronological daily notes for conversation events.
Captures user operating patterns in a dedicated memory file.
Provides qmd commands for semantic, keyword, and vector memory recall.
Keeps project plans separate from personal memory files.
limitations: Requires a writable local agent home directory.
Does not install or configure qmd.
Does not guarantee that stored facts are accurate or current.
Requires periodic review to summarize and supersede stale information.

use_cases.title: Maintain project context
use_cases.description: Store goals, decisions, and durable project facts so future sessions can resume work quickly.

use_cases.title: Track client knowledge
use_cases.description: Organize client preferences and active work into separate entity folders.

use_cases.title: Build a personal research archive
use_cases.description: Capture references and notes in PARA resources, then recall them through search.

prompt_templates.title: Start a memory folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up PARA memory folders under my agent home and explain the purpose of each folder.

prompt_templates.title: Save a durable fact
prompt_templates.prompt: Save this as a durable fact about the Atlas project: its deployment target is Europe West.

prompt_templates.title: Review recent context
prompt_templates.prompt: Search my memory for recent decisions about the Atlas project and summarize the active facts.

prompt_templates.title: Run a memory synthesis
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my daily notes from this week, extract durable facts, update entity summaries, and mark superseded facts.

output_examples.input: Remember that Priya prefers weekly progress updates.
output: Daily note updated with the new preference.
A durable preference fact is added to Priya’s entity record when appropriate.

output_examples.input: What did we decide about the Atlas deployment?
output: Relevant Atlas facts are retrieved from the project memory.
The response distinguishes current decisions from superseded notes.

best_practices: Save only durable, useful facts rather than full conversation transcripts.
Review summaries regularly and mark outdated facts as superseded.
Keep sensitive credentials and private keys out of memory files.
anti_patterns: Do not treat unverified statements as permanent facts.
Do not store every message as an atomic memory item.
Do not delete historical facts when a supersession record preserves context.

faq.question: What is PARA?
faq.answer: PARA organizes information into Projects, Areas, Resources, and Archives.

faq.question: Where does this skill store memory?
faq.answer: It uses folders and files under the configured agent home directory.

faq.question: What belongs in daily notes?
faq.answer: Daily notes hold a chronological record of events and short-lived context.

faq.question: What belongs in an entity file?
faq.answer: Entity files hold durable, specific facts about a project, person, company, or topic.

faq.question: Does this skill search memory automatically?
faq.answer: It provides qmd-based recall instructions, but qmd must be available in the environment.

faq.question: How are outdated facts handled?
faq.answer: Mark them as superseded and link to the newer fact instead of deleting history.
